faq.q: What housing actually exists on Sea Island?
faq.a: Housing is in Burkeville, a pocket of single-detached houses on the south-east part of the island, built for aviation workers in three designs; the City Archives states Burkeville is the only remaining population centre on Sea Island.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Burkeville address?
faq.a: There is no operating school on Sea Island. SD38 catchments are address-based and SD38 has no middle tier; for the sample address 7140 Miller Road the SD38 locator gives Brighouse Elementary and Richmond Secondary — check the exact address in the locator.

faq.q: How does transit serve Sea Island?
faq.a: The Canada Line airport branch stops at Templeton, Sea Island Centre and YVR-Airport stations, with a change at Bridgeport Station for Richmond–Brighouse branch trains.

faq.q: What should a buyer know about aircraft noise on Sea Island?
faq.a: YVR noise is addressed in the YVR 2025–2029 Noise Management Plan, including work to promote compatible land use planning near the airport, and the Airport Authority publishes annual noise reports with monitoring data buyers can review.

faq.q: Who plans land use on Sea Island?
faq.a: Most of the island is federal airport land; the YVR 2037 Master Plan guides land use decision-making and facility development at the airport, and YVR states the airport is on federal lands within the City of Richmond; the Burkeville residential pocket sits inside the City.
